Teaching and mentoring have been a central part of my academic career across the United States and Pakistan. I have taught undergraduate and postgraduate courses across **political science**, **public policy** and **research methods** in both in-person and online settings. Alongside classroom teaching, I have supervised undergraduate and postgraduate research and supported student development through research colloquia, student societies and academic mentoring.

## Teaching approach

My teaching is **student-centred and research-led**. I aim to create an environment in which students actively engage with ideas rather than simply receive information. I use case studies, group work, presentations, debates, role-playing exercises and real-world examples to encourage students to question assumptions, consider different perspectives and apply theoretical concepts to substantive political and policy problems.

I particularly enjoy teaching **research methods**. Rather than presenting methods as a set of technical procedures, I focus on the intuition behind research design and analytical choices: what kinds of questions different approaches can answer, what assumptions they require, and how evidence can be used to evaluate competing explanations. I bring this emphasis on research design and evidence into my substantive teaching as well.

I also see teaching as a collaborative process. I encourage students to contribute their own perspectives and experiences, and use student feedback to reflect on and improve course activities and assessment. My experience teaching across different institutional, cultural and national settings has made me particularly attentive to varied disciplinary backgrounds, learning needs and ways of engaging with academic material.

## GC University Lahore

**Research/Teaching Assistant, 2009–2010 · Lecturer, Department of Political Science, 2010–2017**

I taught **45 sections across 15 undergraduate and postgraduate courses**, involving **1,661 student enrolments** (1,345 undergraduate and 316 postgraduate). My teaching covered research methods, political-system analysis, comparative political institutions and constitutions, foreign policy, political science, international relations and Pakistani politics, delivered through both lecture and seminar formats.

## Research supervision

I supervised **6 MPhil, 8 MA and 15 BA (Hons) research projects involving 39 students**. My supervision has focused on helping students move from broad areas of interest to clearly defined research questions, design feasible studies, select appropriate methods, interpret evidence and communicate their findings clearly.

## Student mentoring & co-curricular engagement

My involvement with students has extended beyond formal classroom teaching and research supervision. At GC University Lahore, I founded the **Parliamentary Student Society** and served as its Faculty Adviser, and also served as **Co-In-Charge of the Quaid-e-Azam Political Science Society**.

I also established and coordinated a **PhD and MPhil Research Colloquium**, providing postgraduate researchers with a regular forum to present developing work, receive feedback and strengthen their research and communication skills. These activities created additional opportunities for students to develop academic confidence, leadership and engagement beyond the formal curriculum.

## Academic and editorial service

Alongside teaching and mentoring, I have contributed to academic publishing, programme development and institutional service. Current and recent roles include **Reviewing Editor, Springer Nature (2026–present)**, **Member of the Editorial Advisory Board, Himalayan Politics (2024–present)** and **Founding Member, Academic Forum, UK Ammonia Alliance (2026–present)**.

Earlier service at GC University Lahore included developing and coordinating academic programmes, coordinating international research collaborations, supporting postgraduate research activities, supervising administrative staff and helping organise major international conferences.
